How much does a website cost in France? The 7 factors that set the price

Two quotes for “a website” can differ tenfold. Here is what really makes the price vary, and the questions to ask before signing.

The Codex teamSoftware studio, Marseille · since 2014
04

Contents0 %

  1. 01The type of website
  2. 02The number of pages and templates

  4. 04Features and integrations

  6. 06SEO and performance
  7. 07Hosting, maintenance and updates
  8. 08How to compare two quotes

Share

In short

  • The price depends on the scope (pages, features, integrations), not on the word “website”.
  • Custom design, content, multiple languages and online payment weigh the most.
  • Compare detailed quotes line by line, including maintenance and hosting.

It is the first question in almost all our meetings: “How much does a website cost?”. The honest answer is that there is no single price, just as there is no single price for “a house”. A five-page business website and an online shop connected to stock have almost nothing in common, apart from their .dz or .com address.

Rather than a price list that would match no real project, here are the seven factors that make a quote vary, and how to read them.

01The type of website

A business website presents your activity, your services and your contact details. An online shop manages a catalogue, a cart, orders and often deliveries. A platform (customer area, booking, marketplace) adds user accounts and business rules. Each level multiplies the design, development and testing work.

02The number of pages and templates

It is not so much the number of pages that matters as the number of different templates. Fifty product pages built on the same model cost less than ten pages that each have their own layout.

03Design: template or custom

A purchased theme lets you start quickly, but it imposes its structure and looks like thousands of other websites. A custom design starts from your brand and your customers: mock-ups, prototypes, approval screen by screen. It takes longer, and it is often what makes the difference in credibility against a competitor.

04Features and integrations

Each feature has a design, development and maintenance cost. The most common ones:

  • advanced forms, appointment booking or online quotes;
  • a customer area with login;
  • online payment and order management;
  • connection to an ERP, a CRM, stock software or a delivery company;
  • an admin dashboard so your team can edit content without a developer.

05Content and languages

Texts, photos, videos: who produces them? A website delivered “empty” costs less at signature, but often delays the launch by several months. In France, many websites must also exist in French and Arabic, sometimes in English. Arabic requires a right-to-left layout, not just a translation.

06SEO and performance

A fast, well-structured website designed for Google from the start costs a little more upfront, but avoids paying for a rebuild later to become visible. Tags, structured data, mobile speed and redirects of old pages are part of a serious quote. Our guide to SEO in France details these points.

07Hosting, maintenance and updates

A website is never “finished”. Security updates, backups, hosting, small changes: always ask what is included after launch, and at what cost.

The cheapest quote is not the one with the smallest total, it is the one that covers everything you will need.

The Codex team

08How to compare two quotes

  1. 01
    Check that both quotes describe the same scope, page by page and feature by feature.
  2. 02
    Ask who will own the code, the domain name and the content.
  3. 03
    Look at the schedule and the approval stages.
  4. 04
    Compare what is planned after launch: training, maintenance, support.
  5. 05
    Ask for verifiable references, for example certificates of good execution.
Codex’s advice

The best way to get an accurate quote is to arrive with a clear need. Our guide to writing a project brief helps you prepare it in an hour.

FAQ

Your questions on this topic

Another question? Write to us, we reply quickly.

Why are website quotes so different?

Because they do not describe the same work. The type of website, custom design or not, the features, the languages, the content and the maintenance make the price vary. Always compare detailed quotes on the same scope.

How long does it take to build a website?

It depends on the scope and on when the content is available. A serious quote includes a phased schedule: scoping, mock-ups, development, testing and launch.

Does the price include hosting and maintenance?

Not always. Ask explicitly what is included after launch: hosting, backups, security updates and changes.
